title: Sneaker Captions Stay Safely Inside
tests: Tests caption accuracy, legibility and explicit safe-area placement throughout a finished vertical product ad.

faults.what: The opening caption garbles “everyday” rather than reproducing the requested text.
All shown captions sit approximately 15% from the top, outside the required central 60% of frame height.
The 5.6-second frame shows a conspicuous ghosted overlap of sneaker views, making the product look doubled during the transition.

judge.summary: The vertical white-sneaker ad has readable captions, but the opening text is garbled and every shown caption violates the requested top safe margin.

must_haves.item: One silent 9:16 video runs for approximately 15 seconds and contains three moving product shots.
must_haves.why: The supplied frames are from one identified 15-second vertical clip and show different product views, but still images cannot establish silence or verify three moving shots.

must_haves.item: The sneaker is consistently a white leather low-top with white laces, a white sole and no logo.
must_haves.why: The visible sneaker consistently has white leather-like uppers, white laces, a white sole, a low-top profile and no identifiable logo.

must_haves.item: The captions read exactly “Meet your everyday pair”, “Clean look. Easy style.” and “Shop now”, in that order.
must_haves.why: The captions occur in the requested sequence, but “everyday” is garbled in the first caption.

must_haves.item: Every visible caption's full bounds stay within the central 70% of frame width and central 60% of frame height, including during transitions.
must_haves.why: The captions occupy roughly 15–19% of frame height, above the permitted region beginning 20% down.

must_haves.item: Captions are legible against the footage and remain visible long enough to read.
must_haves.why: Black text is clearly distinguishable against the plain background, and the middle caption appears at both 5.6 and 9.4 seconds; the sampled frames cannot verify the opening and closing captions' full reading durations.
